title: Candidate Assessment Privacy Notice
intro: This notice explains how House of Marketers uses personal data collected through our candidate work assessment. The assessment is used as one part of our recruitment process and recruitment decisions are made by people, not solely by automated means.

sections.title: 1. Who is responsible for your data?
blocks: INRO GROUP LIMITED, trading as House of Marketers, is the data controller for the personal data covered by this notice.
Company number: 12509530
Registered office: 1 Earlham Street, London, England, WC2H 9LL
Privacy contact: admin@houseofmarketers.com

sections.title: 2. What information do we collect through the assessment?
blocks: We collect only the information reasonably needed to administer and review the assessment, which may include:
your name, email address and the role you applied for;
the assessment version and questions shown to you;
your answers and resulting overall or category scores;
the date and time of the assessment and the time taken to complete it;
assessment integrity information, including the number of times the assessment page loses focus or you switch to another tab or window during the assessment; and
standard technical/security logs generated by our hosting systems, which may include an IP address, browser or device information and timestamps.

The assessment is not designed to diagnose or infer ADHD, dyslexia, autism, neurodivergence, disability or any other health condition. Please do not enter medical or disability information into assessment answer fields.

sections.title: 3. Why do we use this information?
blocks: We use assessment data to:
administer a work-related recruitment assessment;
assess role-relevant skills such as accuracy, prioritisation, numerical reasoning, logical reasoning and operational judgement;
support our recruiters and hiring managers in making recruitment decisions;
protect the security and reliability of the assessment process;
support the integrity of the assessment and help our recruitment team identify assessment activity that may require human review;
keep appropriate records of recruitment decisions and respond to queries or legal claims; and
after anonymisation, analyse and improve the effectiveness of our assessment process.
Tab or window switching is not used as an automatic reason to reject a candidate.

sections.title: 4. Our lawful basis
blocks: We process ordinary recruitment and assessment data on the basis of our legitimate interests under Article 6(1)(f) UK GDPR. Our legitimate interest is assessing candidates fairly and effectively for roles at House of Marketers and maintaining the integrity of our recruitment process.
We have carried out a Legitimate Interests Assessment to consider the necessity and impact of this processing.
We do not rely on consent as the lawful basis for the ordinary assessment data described in this notice.

Where health or disability information is processed for recruitment adjustments, we rely on the relevant employment-law obligations and the applicable special-category condition under UK data protection law.

sections.title: 5. Reasonable adjustments and health information
blocks: If you voluntarily provide health or disability information in order to request a reasonable adjustment, we process that information only for the purpose of considering and providing that adjustment. This information is handled separately from assessment scoring and is not used to disadvantage your application.
The assessment application itself does not record your diagnosis or the reason for an adjustment.

sections.title: 6. Who can access or receive your information?
blocks: Access is limited to people and organisations that need the information for the purposes described above. This may include:
authorised House of Marketers recruitment, operations and hiring staff;
external recruitment partners involved in the relevant hiring process, where applicable;
cloud hosting, database, IT and security providers acting on our behalf; and
professional advisers, regulators, courts or public authorities where disclosure is required or permitted by law.
We do not sell candidate assessment data.

sections.title: 7. International transfers
blocks: Our service providers may process personal data in the UK, the EEA or other countries. If personal data is transferred outside the UK and UK data protection law requires transfer safeguards, we will use an appropriate lawful transfer mechanism before making that transfer, such as UK adequacy regulations or approved contractual safeguards.

sections.title: 8. How long do we keep the assessment data?
blocks: Identifiable assessment data for unsuccessful candidates is normally retained for six months after the recruitment outcome. After that period, it is deleted or genuinely anonymised. Information may be retained for longer where reasonably necessary in connection with an actual or anticipated complaint or legal claim.
If you are hired, any information that needs to be retained separately as part of your employment record is governed by our employee data-retention arrangements rather than this assessment system.

sections.title: 9. Is taking the assessment mandatory?
blocks: There is no statutory requirement to provide assessment data. However, where this assessment forms part of the selection process for a role, we may be unable to progress your application if you choose not to complete it.

sections.title: 10. Automated decision-making
blocks: House of Marketers does not make recruitment decisions about you solely by automated means. Assessment results are reviewed by a recruiter or hiring manager and are considered as part of the wider recruitment process.

sections.title: 11. Your data protection rights
blocks: Depending on the circumstances and the lawful basis being used, you may have rights to:
request access to the personal data we hold about you;
ask us to correct inaccurate or incomplete personal data;
ask us to erase your personal data in certain circumstances;
ask us to restrict processing in certain circumstances;
object to processing based on legitimate interests; and
request data portability where that right applies.
These rights are not absolute and may be subject to legal conditions or exemptions. To exercise a right or ask a privacy question, contact admin@houseofmarketers.com.
Your right to object: Where we rely on legitimate interests, you have the right to object to that processing. We will consider your objection in accordance with UK data protection law.

sections.title: 12. Complaints
blocks: If you have concerns about how we use your personal data, please contact us first at admin@houseofmarketers.com so we can try to resolve the issue.
You also have the right to complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO), the UK supervisory authority for data protection. Information about making a complaint is available at ico.org.uk.

sections.title: 13. Changes to this notice
blocks: We may update this notice if the assessment process, technology, service providers or applicable law changes. The version made available when you take the assessment will state its effective date.
